name: Asim Mohamed
description: Machine learning researcher working on AI security, content provenance and watermarking, the safety of AI agents, and trustworthy multilingual NLP.
researchInterests: AI security and adversarial robustness of LLMs
Safety of AI agents and agentic automation
Evaluation and red-teaming of language models
bio:
I am a machine learning researcher working on AI security, content provenance, and the safety of language models and the agents built on top of them. I hold a master's in Machine Intelligence from the African Master's in Machine Intelligence (AMMI) at AIMS, where my thesis on multilingual LLM watermarking was supervised by Dr. Martin Gubri of Parameter Lab.

The through-line of my work is whether safety guarantees hold up outside English. My papers show that multilingual LLM watermarks can be erased by a simple back-translation attack, predict Arabic readability with hybrid BERT and linguistic features, and establish the first Coptic-centred corpus for machine translation. I am currently surveying adversarial vulnerabilities and prompt-injection attacks in multilingual and low-resource models.

I also work as a senior AI engineer building production LLM agents and retrieval systems, which keeps my research close to the failure modes that actually reach users. Before AMMI I read electrical and electronic engineering at the University of Khartoum. The fastest way to reach me is by email.
